span.label: critique
span.quote: In particular, we will see that the so-called “model-free” methods popular in deep reinforcement learning are considerably less effective in both theory and practice than simple model-based schemes when applied to LQR.

span.label: reinforcement learning for continuous control
span.quote: With a focus on problems in continuous control, I will try to disentangle the similarities and differences of methods of the complementary perspectives and present a set of challenging problems whose solution will require significant input from both sets of practitioners.

span.label: review
span.quote: This survey aims to provide a language for the control and reinforcement learning communities to begin communicating, highlighting what each can learn from the other.

span.label: significant challenges remain at the control-learning interface
span.quote: Challenges at the control-learning interface

span.label: The survey deliberately stays at the level of conceptual ideas and omits the technical detail needed to make its statements precise.
span.quote: Throughout, my aim will be to highlight the main conceptual ideas of different approaches and to avoid embroiling myself in a thorough discussion of the myriad of technical details required to make all of the statements crisply precise.

span.label: The scope is restricted to episodic RL and excludes the harder adaptive-control setting.
span.quote: This survey has focused on “episodic” reinforcement learning and has steered clear of a much harder problem: adaptive control.

span.label: The theoretical comparison between value-function estimation and model estimation rests on worst-case upper bounds, which the author concedes is not a valid comparison.
span.quote: While comparing worst-case upper bounds is certainly not valid, it is suggestive that, as mentioned above, temporal differencing methods use only one defining equation per time step whereas model estimation uses d equations per time step.

span.label: Function approximation, and deep RL specifically, is set aside rather than analysed.
span.quote: Note that in this section I have spent no time discussing deep reinforcement learning.

span.label: The empirical evidence rests on a small set of simulation benchmarks that invite overfitting.
span.quote: Benchmarking is difficult, and having only a few simulation benchmarks encourages overfitting to these benchmarks.

span.label: The label model-free does not mean the method is free of modelling; the author says modelling is heavily built into its assumptions.
span.quote: modeling is not heavily built into the assumptions of model-free RL algorithms

span.label: A discounting device had to be introduced to obtain a tractable equation, and the author names that as troubling.
span.quote: Also troubling is the fact that we had to introduce the discount factor in order to get a simple Bellman equation

span.label: The scope claimed for the field is stated to be precisely the scope of a different, older field.
span.quote: A control engineer might be puzzled by such a definition and interject that this is precisely the scope of control theory

span.label: framing and analyzing reinforcement learning with the tools of optimal control, using the Linear Quadratic Regulator as the baseline
span.quote: the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) with unknown dynamics, perhaps the simplest and best-studied problem in optimal control

span.label: random search - THE SAME METHOD UNDER FOUR NAMES: pure random search in RL, a (mu,lambda) Evolution Strategy in evolutionary computation, and studied again under stochastic approximation and under bandits - four literatures, one procedure, and this paper is where they are listed
span.quote: Random search was also discovered by the evolutionary algorithms community, where it is called a (µ, λ)-Evolution Strategy [15, 66]. Random search has also been studied in the context of stochastic approximation

span.label: model-free - A LABEL THAT DENIES WHAT THE METHOD CARRIES: the name marks the absence of an explicit dynamics model while the modelling assumptions remain, built into the algorithm
